newsitem.title: USA: FCC proposes more open U.S. telecom markets.
newsitem.headline: FCC proposes more open U.S. telecom markets.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday said it planned to liberalise access to U.S. telecommunications markets for most foreign companies, in line with World Trade Organization (WTO) rules.

Among measures the FCC said it will be proposing is the elimination of the Effective Competitive Opportunities (ECO) test, which requires that a foreign country give equivalent access to U.S. companies before firms from that country can operate in the U.S. telecommunications market.

"The commission tentatively concludes that competition in the U.S. market will be best served by eliminating the burdensome ECO analysis and instead granting ... applications on a streamlined basis," the FCC said in a statement.

The FCC said its proposed new rules would be more appropriate in the liberalised environment that will exist when the recent WTO agreement on basic telecommunications services takes effect on January 1, 1998.
